items.name: Basilisk
items.desc: Basilisk is a dragon from European/Arabic mythology. Described by Pliny the Elder and later Christian bestiaries, the Basilisk is a small but deadly serpent crown-crested creature whose mere gaze causes death. It is said to be hatched from a cock's egg incubated by a serpent or toad. In Christian symbology adopted by the Vatican, the Basilisk represents the power of sin and heresy that can be overcome by faith. Medieval bestiaries often used the Basilisk as a symbol of the Antichrist, and its deadly gaze represented the corrupting power of evil

items.name: The Universal Basilisk
items.desc: A legendary serpent or dragon, the Basilisk is known as the king of serpents, with a gaze and breath so venomous it can kill anything it encounters.

items.name: Werewolf
items.desc: Werewolf (Generic). is a shapeshifter. A human who transforms into a wolf, either voluntarily or by curse. Source: European folklore, global shapeshifting myths
